+﻿function Test-MtEntraUnremediatedMediumRiskUser {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Finds users that Entra ID Protection rates medium risk and that nobody has remediated.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Entra ID Protection flags users it believes may be compromised and assigns a risk level and a
+    risk state. A flag only clears when someone remediates it (password reset) or an admin
+    dismisses or confirms-safe it. This check reports users whose risk level is medium and whose
+    risk state still shows active, unremediated risk, so an admin can act on flags that have been
+    left sitting. If a reported user holds a privileged directory role, it is listed first
+    with its roles. It reads risk only; it never changes a user's risk state.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Test-MtEntraUnremediatedMediumRiskUser
+
+    .LINK
+    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtEntraUnremediatedMediumRiskUser
+
+    .LINK
+    https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/riskyuser?view=graph-rest-1.0
+    #>
+    [MaesterTest(
+        Id = 'MT.1261',
+        Title = 'Medium-risk users should not be left unremediated in Entra ID Protection.',
+        Product = 'entra',
+        Feature = 'identity-protection',
+        Area = 'logging-and-detection',
+        ResourceType = 'User',
+        Severity = 'Low',
+        UserImpact = 'Low',
+        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
+        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
+        Control = ('nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(12)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IR-4'),
+        Cloud = ('Commercial', 'GCC', 'GCCHigh', 'DoD'),
+        Service = 'Graph',
+        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM_P2',
+        Permission = ('Graph:Scope:IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:RoleManagement.Read.Directory|Graph:Scope:RoleManagement.Read.All'),
+        Lifecycle = 'Preview',
+        Author = 'Dfrank77'
+    )]
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([bool])]
+    param()
+
+    # Deleted users stay in the risk report and admins cannot dismiss them, so they are not reported.
+    # Active, unremediated risk states. A flag an admin has handled moves to 'remediated',
+    # 'dismissed', 'confirmedSafe' or 'none'; those are intentionally excluded.
+    # 'confirmedCompromised' MUST be treated as unremediated alongside 'atRisk' -- confirming a
+    # user compromised does not clear the risk.
+    $UnremediatedStates = @('atRisk', 'confirmedCompromised')
+
+    Write-Verbose 'Reading medium-risk users from Entra ID Protection.'
+    # Filter riskLevel server-side only. The riskState set is applied client-side on purpose:
+    # Graph rejects some compound / 'or' / 'in' filter shapes on this endpoint, so a single-property
+    # filter is the reliable shape, and the state list is tiny to post-filter.
+    try {
+        $MediumRiskUsers = @(
+            Invoke-MtGraphRequest -ApiVersion 'v1.0' `
+                -RelativeUri 'identityProtection/riskyUsers' `
+                -Filter "riskLevel eq 'medium'" `
+                -Select @('id', 'isDeleted', 'userPrincipalName', 'userDisplayName', 'riskLevel', 'riskState', 'riskDetail', 'riskLastUpdatedDateTime')
+        )
+    } catch {
+        if ($_.Exception.Message -match '(?i)403|forbidden|authorization') {
+            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized
+            return $null
+        }
+        throw
+    }
+
+    $Unremediated = @(
+        $MediumRiskUsers | Where-Object { $UnremediatedStates -contains [string]$_.riskState -and $_.isDeleted -ne $true }
+    )
+    Write-Verbose "Found $($MediumRiskUsers.Count) medium-risk user(s); $($Unremediated.Count) unremediated."
+
+    if ($Unremediated.Count -eq 0) {
+        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result (
+            'Well done. No medium-risk users are left unremediated in Entra ID Protection.'
+        )
+        return $true
+    }
+
+    # Privileged users at risk are listed first with their roles (#2518). Roles are only read when
+    # there is something to report, so a clean tenant makes no extra Graph calls. The role lookup is extra
+    # detail: if it fails, the unremediated users are still reported, with a note.
+    $PrivilegedRolesByUser = @{}
+    $RoleNote = ''
+    try {
+        $RoleDefinitions = @(
+            Invoke-MtGraphRequest -ApiVersion 'v1.0' `
+                -RelativeUri 'roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions' `
+                -Select @('id', 'displayName')
+        )
+        $RoleDefLookup = @{}
+        foreach ($Def in $RoleDefinitions) { $RoleDefLookup[[string]$Def.id] = $Def }
+
+        # Same properties as MT.1209 and MT.1210 so the active assignments come from the Graph cache.
+        $RoleAssignmentResult = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -Select @('id', 'principalId', 'roleDefinitionId', 'directoryScopeId')
+        if (!$RoleAssignmentResult.EligibleChecked) {
+            $RoleNote = "`n`nNote: PIM-eligible role assignments were not checked because they need " +
+                'Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Governance. Only active role assignments were checked.'
+        }
+
+        $UnremediatedIds = @{}
+        foreach ($Item in $Unremediated) { $UnremediatedIds[[string]$Item.id] = $true }
+
+        foreach ($Assignment in @($RoleAssignmentResult.Assignments)) {
+            $PrincipalId = [string]$Assignment.principalId
+            if (!$UnremediatedIds.ContainsKey($PrincipalId)) { continue }
+            $RoleDef = $RoleDefLookup[[string]$Assignment.roleDefinitionId]
+            if ($null -eq $RoleDef) { continue }
+            # isPrivileged is not queryable on roleDefinitions; use Maester's role catalog, as MT.1210 does.
+            $RoleInfo = Get-MtRoleInfo -RoleName ([string]$RoleDef.displayName -replace '\s', '')
+            if ($null -eq $RoleInfo -or !$RoleInfo.IsPrivileged) { continue }
+            $RoleName = [string]$RoleDef.displayName
+            if ($Assignment.AssignmentType -eq 'Eligible') { $RoleName += ' (eligible)' }
+            if (!$PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey($PrincipalId)) {
+                $PrivilegedRolesByUser[$PrincipalId] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
+            }
+            $PrivilegedRolesByUser[$PrincipalId].Add($RoleName)
+        }
+    } catch {
+        Write-Verbose "Could not read directory role assignments: $($_.Exception.Message)"
+        $PrivilegedRolesByUser = @{}
+        $RoleNote = "`n`nNote: Directory role assignments could not be read, so privileged users were not identified."
+    }
+
+    # Privileged users first, then by user principal name.
+    $Sorted = @(
+        $Unremediated | Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { -not $PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey([string]$_.id) } }, userPrincipalName
+    )
+    $PrivilegedCount = @($Unremediated | Where-Object { $PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey([string]$_.id) }).Count
+
+    $Result = "Found $($Unremediated.Count) medium-risk user(s) with unremediated risk."
+    if ($PrivilegedCount -gt 0) {
+        $Result += " $PrivilegedCount of them hold a privileged directory role and are listed first."
+    }
+    $Result += "`n`n| User | User principal name | Risk state | Risk detail | Risk last updated | Privileged role |"
+    $Result += "`n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"
+    foreach ($Item in $Sorted) {
+        $DisplayName = [string]$Item.userDisplayName
+        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($DisplayName)) { $DisplayName = '(unnamed)' }
+        $DisplayName = Get-MtSafeMarkdown $DisplayName
+        $Upn = Get-MtSafeMarkdown ([string]$Item.userPrincipalName)
+        $State = [string]$Item.riskState
+        $Detail = Get-MtSafeMarkdown ([string]$Item.riskDetail)
+        $Updated = if ($Item.riskLastUpdatedDateTime) {
+            ($Item.riskLastUpdatedDateTime -as [datetime]).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
+        } else { 'Unknown' }
+        $Roles = if ($PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey([string]$Item.id)) {
+            Get-MtSafeMarkdown ($PrivilegedRolesByUser[[string]$Item.id] -join ', ')
+        } else { 'None' }
+        $Result += "`n| $DisplayName | $Upn | $State | $Detail | $Updated | $Roles |"
+    }
+    $Result += $RoleNote
+
+    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $Result
+    return $false
+}

A value that does not match the kind's pattern (for example a malformed GUID) is `InvalidConfiguration`. In the
config a value can be the ID itself or an object `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }`; the test always
receives the ID.

## Families: one test, several results

Some checks produce one result per item: per drift folder, per recommendation, per user. Declare
`InstanceSource` with the name of a function in the same file. The engine calls that function when the test
runs (never during discovery) and runs the test once per object it returns, passing the object as `$Instance`.

```powershell
function Get-ContosoAdminUnit {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    foreach ($unit in Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'directory/administrativeUnits') {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id    = $unit.id                     # required: the instance suffix
            Title = "Administrative unit '$($unit.displayName)' is restricted"   # optional
            Data  = $unit                        # optional: anything the test needs
        }
    }
}

function Test-ContosoAdminUnitRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CONTOSO.2001',
        Title = 'Administrative units are restricted.',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        Service = 'Graph',
        InstanceSource = 'Get-ContosoAdminUnit'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The administrative unit to check, supplied by the engine.
        $Instance
    )

    $restricted = [bool]$Instance.Data.isMemberManagementRestricted
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Member management restricted: $restricted"
    return $restricted
}
```

The instance object has:

| Property | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | Yes | The suffix. The row's ID is `<parent ID>.<Id>`, for example `CONTOSO.2001.4f6c...`. It must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$` and be unique within the family. |
| `Title` | No | The instance's title. Defaults to `-TestTitle` from the helper, then the attribute's title. |
| `Severity` | No | The instance's severity, used when the config sets none. |
| `Tag` | No | Extra tags written to the instance's row. |
| `Fields` | No | Facts about the instance that a report can group or filter by, as a hashtable of names to strings or arrays of strings, for example `@{ Pillar = 'Identity'; Category = 'Access control' }`. Written to the row's `Fields`; other values are left out. |
| `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `RelatedProduct`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` | No | What this instance is about, when that differs from its family, with the same keys as the attribute. A family that reads results from another tool, such as the Zero Trust Assessment pack, places each result under its own product this way. A value the taxonomy does not know is left out, and the row keeps the family's. |
| `Data` | No | Anything the test needs. It is not written to the result. |

Each instance row carries `ParentId` (the family's ID) and `InstanceId`. When the family does not produce
instance rows, the result has one row on the parent ID instead:

| What happened | Row on the parent ID |
| --- | --- |
| The family was not selected, was disabled, or a gate failed | The usual `NotRun` or `Skipped` reason |
| The instance source returned nothing | `Skipped` with `NoInstances` |
| The instance source threw, did not finish within the family's timeout, or ended with `exit` | `Error` with `InstanceSourceFailed` |
| An instance `Id` is missing, invalid or repeated | `Error` with `InvalidInstanceId` |

The instance source runs under the same timeout as the test (the family's `TimeoutSeconds`, or the run's
`Execution` timeout). The source gets that long to return, and then each instance gets that long to run.

Selection and configuration understand families:

- `-TestId CONTOSO.2001` or `-TestId 'CONTOSO.2001.*'` selects the whole family.
- `-TestId CONTOSO.2001.abc` runs only that instance; the others get `NotRun` rows with reason `NotSelected`.
- `-ExcludeTestId` and `"Enabled": false` on an instance ID drop that instance after the source has run.
- A `TestSettings` row on an instance ID wins over a row on the parent ID. Its `Parameters` and
  `TimeoutSeconds` apply to that instance only; a parameter it does not name keeps the value of the family's row.
- IDs under a family's parent are never reported as unknown, even if that instance does not exist in this run.

## Settings shared by many tests

Read tenant-wide settings from `GlobalSettings` in the config with `Get-MtSetting`:

+﻿function Test-MtEntraUnremediatedHighRiskServicePrincipal {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Finds service principals that Entra ID Protection rates high risk and that nobody has remediated.
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Entra ID Protection flags service principals (workload identities) it believes are compromised
+    and assigns a risk level and a risk state. A flag only clears when an admin remediates or
+    dismisses it. This check reports service principals whose risk level is
+    high and whose risk state still shows active, unremediated risk, so an admin can act on flags
+    that have been left sitting. If a reported service principal holds a privileged directory role,
+    it is listed first with its roles. It reads risk only; it never changes a service principal's risk state.
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Test-MtEntraUnremediatedHighRiskServicePrincipal
+    .LINK
+    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtEntraUnremediatedHighRiskServicePrincipal
+    .LINK
+    https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/riskyserviceprincipal?view=graph-rest-1.0
+    #>
+    [MaesterTest(
+        Id = 'MT.1262',
+        Title = 'High-risk service principals should not be left unremediated in Entra ID Protection.',
+        Product = 'entra',
+        Feature = 'identity-protection',
+        Area = 'applications',
+        ResourceType = 'ServicePrincipal',
+        Severity = 'Medium',
+        UserImpact = 'Low',
+        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
+        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
+        Control = ('nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(12)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IR-4'),
+        Cloud = ('Commercial', 'GCC', 'GCCHigh', 'DoD'),
+        Service = 'Graph',
+        License = ('AAD_WRKLDID_P1', 'AAD_WRKLDID_P2'),
+        Permission = ('Graph:Scope:IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:RoleManagement.Read.Directory|Graph:Scope:RoleManagement.Read.All'),
+        Lifecycle = 'Preview',
+        Author = 'Dfrank77'
+    )]
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([bool])]
+    param()
+
+    # Active, unremediated risk states, same as MT.1260. 'confirmedCompromised' is still unremediated:
+    # confirming a service principal compromised does not clear the risk, and the confirmCompromised
+    # API (the documented way to simulate risk for testing) lands service principals in this state.
+    $UnremediatedStates = @('atRisk', 'confirmedCompromised')
+
+    Write-Verbose 'Reading high-risk service principals from Entra ID Protection.'
+    # Filter riskLevel server-side only and apply the riskState set client-side, same as MT.1260.
+    try {
+        $HighRiskServicePrincipals = @(
+            Invoke-MtGraphRequest -ApiVersion 'v1.0' `
+                -RelativeUri 'identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals' `
+                -Filter "riskLevel eq 'high'" `
+                -Select @('id', 'appId', 'displayName', 'servicePrincipalType', 'riskLevel', 'riskState', 'riskDetail', 'riskLastUpdatedDateTime')
+        )
+    } catch {
+        if ($_.Exception.Message -match '(?i)403|forbidden|authorization') {
+            Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized
+            return $null
+        }
+        throw
+    }
+
+    $Unremediated = @(
+        $HighRiskServicePrincipals | Where-Object { $UnremediatedStates -contains [string]$_.riskState }
+    )
+    Write-Verbose "Found $($HighRiskServicePrincipals.Count) high-risk service principal(s); $($Unremediated.Count) unremediated."
+
+    if ($Unremediated.Count -eq 0) {
+        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result (
+            'Well done. No high-risk service principals are left unremediated in Entra ID Protection.'
+        )
+        return $true
+    }
+
+    # Service principals at risk that hold a privileged role are listed first with their roles, as MT.1260 does
+    # for users. Roles are only read when there is something to report. If the lookup fails, the
+    # unremediated service principals are still reported, with a note.
+    $PrivilegedRolesBySp = @{}
+    $RoleNote = ''
+    try {
+        $RoleDefinitions = @(
+            Invoke-MtGraphRequest -ApiVersion 'v1.0' `
+                -RelativeUri 'roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions' `
+                -Select @('id', 'displayName')
+        )
+        $RoleDefLookup = @{}
+        foreach ($Def in $RoleDefinitions) { $RoleDefLookup[[string]$Def.id] = $Def }
+
+        # Same properties as MT.1209, MT.1210 and MT.1260 so the active assignments come from the Graph cache.
+        $RoleAssignmentResult = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -Select @('id', 'principalId', 'roleDefinitionId', 'directoryScopeId')
+        if (!$RoleAssignmentResult.EligibleChecked) {
+            $RoleNote = "`n`nNote: PIM-eligible role assignments were not checked because they need " +
+                'Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Governance. Only active role assignments were checked.'
+        }
+
+        $UnremediatedIds = @{}
+        foreach ($Item in $Unremediated) { $UnremediatedIds[[string]$Item.id] = $true }
+
+        foreach ($Assignment in @($RoleAssignmentResult.Assignments)) {
+            $PrincipalId = [string]$Assignment.principalId
+            if (!$UnremediatedIds.ContainsKey($PrincipalId)) { continue }
+            $RoleDef = $RoleDefLookup[[string]$Assignment.roleDefinitionId]
+            if ($null -eq $RoleDef) { continue }
+            $RoleInfo = Get-MtRoleInfo -RoleName ([string]$RoleDef.displayName -replace '\s', '')
+            if ($null -eq $RoleInfo -or !$RoleInfo.IsPrivileged) { continue }
+            $RoleName = [string]$RoleDef.displayName
+            if ($Assignment.AssignmentType -eq 'Eligible') { $RoleName += ' (eligible)' }
+            if (!$PrivilegedRolesBySp.ContainsKey($PrincipalId)) {
+                $PrivilegedRolesBySp[$PrincipalId] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
+            }
+            $PrivilegedRolesBySp[$PrincipalId].Add($RoleName)
+        }
+    } catch {
+        Write-Verbose "Could not read directory role assignments: $($_.Exception.Message)"
+        $PrivilegedRolesBySp = @{}
+        $RoleNote = "`n`nNote: Directory role assignments could not be read, so privileged service principals were not identified."
+    }
+
+    # Privileged service principals first, then by display name.
+    $Sorted = @(
+        $Unremediated | Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { -not $PrivilegedRolesBySp.ContainsKey([string]$_.id) } }, displayName
+    )
+    $PrivilegedCount = @($Unremediated | Where-Object { $PrivilegedRolesBySp.ContainsKey([string]$_.id) }).Count
+
+    $Result = "Found $($Unremediated.Count) high-risk service principal(s) with unremediated risk."
+    if ($PrivilegedCount -gt 0) {
+        $Result += " $PrivilegedCount of them hold a privileged directory role and are listed first."
+    }
+    $Result += "`n`n| Service principal | Application ID | Type | Risk state | Risk detail | Risk last updated | Privileged role |"
+    $Result += "`n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"
+    foreach ($Item in $Sorted) {
+        $DisplayName = [string]$Item.displayName
+        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($DisplayName)) { $DisplayName = '(unnamed)' }
+        $Link = Get-MtLinkServicePrincipal -ServicePrincipal ([pscustomobject]@{ id = $Item.id; appId = $Item.appId; DisplayName = $DisplayName })
+        $Type = Get-MtSafeMarkdown ([string]$Item.servicePrincipalType)
+        $State = [string]$Item.riskState
+        $Detail = Get-MtSafeMarkdown ([string]$Item.riskDetail)
+        $Updated = if ($Item.riskLastUpdatedDateTime) {
+            ($Item.riskLastUpdatedDateTime -as [datetime]).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
+        } else { 'Unknown' }
+        $Roles = if ($PrivilegedRolesBySp.ContainsKey([string]$Item.id)) {
+            Get-MtSafeMarkdown ($PrivilegedRolesBySp[[string]$Item.id] -join ', ')
+        } else { 'None' }
+        $Result += "`n| $Link | $($Item.appId) | $Type | $State | $Detail | $Updated | $Roles |"
+    }
+    $Result += $RoleNote
+
+    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $Result
+    return $false
+}

diff --git a/powershell/public/connect/Get-MtGraphScope.ps1 b/powershell/public/connect/Get-MtGraphScope.ps1 index 5d2f7fc8c..e6ba65025 100644 --- a/powershell/public/connect/Get-MtGraphScope.ps1 +++ b/powershell/public/connect/Get-MtGraphScope.ps1 @@ -100,6 +100,7 @@ 'AgentIdentityBlueprintPrincipal.Read.All' 'Application.Read.All' 'IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All' + 'SecurityEvents.Read.All' ) if ($IncludePreview) { diff --git a/tests/maester/defender/Test.MT.1264.md b/tests/maester/defender/Test.MT.1264.md new file mode 100644 index 000000000..4c8266cdc --- /dev/null +++ b/tests/maester/defender/Test.MT.1264.md @@ -0,0 +1,24 @@ +Microsoft Secure Score improvement actions should be completed. + +Microsoft Secure Score measures a tenant's security posture as points earned across a list of recommended improvement actions, such as requiring multifactor authentication for administrators or turning on Safe Links. Maester reads the tenant's latest Secure Score and creates one result per improvement action the tenant is scored on (MT.1264.<control name>). Improvement actions that are not part of the tenant's score are not reported. + +These results are not native Maester checks. The improvement actions, their points and the status details come from Microsoft Secure Score. A change made in the tenant usually takes 24 to 48 hours to show in Secure Score, and some Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Entra improvement actions refresh less often. + +An improvement action passes when it has all of its points and fails when it has fewer, showing the points earned. The severity of each result comes from the action's maximum points: 8 or more is High, 4 to 7 is Medium, and below 4 is Low. Improvement actions that an administrator has set to **Risk accepted**, **Resolved through third party** or **Resolved through alternate mitigation** in the Microsoft Defender portal, or that carry the older **Reviewed** state, are skipped, with the status, who set it and their note, so decisions already made in the portal are respected. Improvement actions set to **Planned** are still checked, since the work is not done yet. + +Some improvement actions, such as multifactor authentication for administrators, are also Entra recommendations reported by MT.1024. Maester matches them by name against the tenant's Entra recommendations, and those results note the overlap. + +The check needs the Microsoft Graph permission `SecurityEvents.Read.All`, which Maester does not request by default. Without it the check is skipped. Connect with `Connect-Maester -IncludePreview`, or grant the permission to the app registration that runs Maester. + +#### Remediation action + +Open each failed improvement action in the [Microsoft Secure Score](https://security.microsoft.com/securescore) page of the Microsoft Defender portal and follow its implementation steps. If an improvement action does not apply to your tenant, or is already covered by another product, set its status to **Risk accepted**, **Resolved through third party** or **Resolved through alternate mitigation** in the Defender portal; Maester then skips it on the next run. Improvement actions in the Device category can't be given a status there; Microsoft directs you to the matching Defender Vulnerability Management recommendation instead. + +#### Related links + +- [Microsoft Secure Score](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/microsoft-secure-score) +- [Assess your security posture with Microsoft Secure Score](https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/microsoft-secure-score-improvement-actions) +- [Microsoft Secure Score - Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com/securescore) + + +%TestResult% diff --git a/tests/maester/defender/Test.MT.1264.ps1 b/tests/maester/defender/Test.MT.1264.ps1 new file mode 100644 index 000000000..8805edb77 --- /dev/null +++ b/tests/maester/defender/Test.MT.1264.ps1 @@ -0,0 +1,259 @@ +﻿function Get-MtSecureScoreControlInstance { + <# + .SYNOPSIS + Returns one MT.1264 instance per Microsoft Secure Score control the tenant is scored on. + + .DESCRIPTION + Instance source of the MT.1264 family. The instances come from controlScores in the latest Secure + Score snapshot, not from the full secureScoreControlProfiles catalog: the catalog lists every control + Microsoft has (including ones for products the tenant does not use), while the snapshot lists only the + controls the tenant is actually scored on. Each control is joined to its profile for the title, the + maximum points and the remediation. The suffix is the control name (MT.1264.) and the + severity comes from the control's maximum points. + #> + [CmdletBinding()] + [OutputType([pscustomobject])] + param() + + try { + # Only the latest daily snapshot. Without -DisablePaging the helper would follow nextLink through + # up to 90 days of history. + $snapshotResponse = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'security/secureScores' -QueryParameters @{ '$top' = 1 } -DisablePaging + $snapshot = @($snapshotResponse.value) | Select-Object -First 1 + $profiles = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'security/secureScoreControlProfiles') + } catch { + if ($_.Exception.Message -match '(?i)403|forbidden|authorization') { + Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized + return + } + throw + } + + # No snapshot yet (for example a brand new tenant): no instances, so the engine skips the family. + if ($null -eq $snapshot) { return } + + $profileLookup = @{} + foreach ($controlProfile in $profiles) { $profileLookup[[string]$controlProfile.id] = $controlProfile } + + # Entra recommendations MT.1024 already reports. Some Secure Score controls are the same recommendation + # under the same name (AdminMFAV2 and adminMFAV2), so those results say so. Matched by name, not by the + # control's service: not every AzureAD control is an Entra recommendation. Same request as MT.1024, so + # it comes from the Graph cache when MT.1024 has run. If it fails, the results just carry no note. + $entraRecommendationTypes = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) + try { + $recommendations = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -ApiVersion beta -RelativeUri 'directory/recommendations?$expand=impactedResources' -OutputType Hashtable + foreach ($recommendation in @($recommendations.value)) { + if ($recommendation -and $recommendation.recommendationType) { [void]$entraRecommendationTypes.Add([string]$recommendation.recommendationType) } + } + } catch { + Write-Verbose "MT.1264: could not read Entra recommendations, so no result notes the overlap with MT.1024. $($_.Exception.Message)" + } + + foreach ($controlScore in @($snapshot.controlScores)) { + $controlName = [string]$controlScore.controlName + $controlProfile = $profileLookup[$controlName] + if ($controlProfile.deprecated) { continue } + # A scored control with no profile has no maximum to compare against. ## Severity

The risk to the organization while the test fails. Not the effort to fix it and not the disruption of fixing it.

| Value | A failing result means |
| --- | --- |
| `Critical` | An attacker with no special position can take over the tenant, the domain or a privileged identity, or a secret is already exposed. Directly exploitable and wide in reach. |
| `High` | A primary control is missing or weakened for many users or for privileged identities, and common techniques such as phishing, password spray or consent phishing are enough to use it. |
| `Medium` | A defence-in-depth control is missing, or the exposure is limited to a few objects or one workload, or using it needs another weakness first. |
| `Low` | Hardening or hygiene with a small security effect on its own. |
| `Info` | The test reports a fact for review and makes no risk judgement. Info tests are left out of scores. |

Decide in this order:

1. **Reach.** Privileged identities or the whole tenant move the value up. A single workload or a few objects
   move it down.
2. **Directness.** Usable from the internet or by any signed-in user moves it up. Needing an earlier compromise
   moves it down. A password taken by phishing, spray or stuffing is not an earlier compromise: those are the
   common techniques `High` already assumes.
3. **Role of the control.** The main control for a threat rates higher than a second layer behind another control.

`Critical` is rare. If the description cannot say in one sentence how an attacker gets from the failing state to
admin rights or exposed secrets, the value is `High` or lower. A benchmark's own wording does not set the value:
a SHALL policy can be `Medium`.

Five cases come up often:

- **A test that passes whenever its data can be read** is `Info`, whatever the data is about. If the fact
  deserves a severity, the test should fail on it.
- **A failure that is only an outage or untidiness**, such as replication health, an expiring token or an unused

## ImplementationCost

How much administrator work the recommended fix takes.

| Value | The fix is |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | One setting or one policy in one portal. Under an hour, with no dependency on another team, a licence purchase or a rollout. |
| `Medium` | Several steps: a policy that needs exclusions and a pilot, clean-up of a handful of objects, coordination with one other team. Hours to a few days. |
| `High` | A project: new licences, infrastructure or process, a migration of users or apps, or clean-up across many objects. Weeks or more. |

Clean-up that one administrator can finish alone in a sitting is `Low`. Clean-up that needs the owner of each
object is `Medium`. Turning on a plan that is billed by use is `Medium`: the click is easy, the budget approval is
not. Count the work of the fix, including exclusions and rollout, but not the time to decide.

Omit `ImplementationCost` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## Mitre

The MITRE ATT&CK techniques that the checked control prevents or detects. A list of technique IDs, or `None`.

- IDs only, in the form `T1110` or `T1110.003`. Tactic names are looked up from the pinned ATT&CK release
  (`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`) and are never typed.
- Use a sub-technique when the control addresses only that sub-technique. When three or more sub-techniques of
  one technique apply, list the technique instead. Do not list a technique together with one of its own
  sub-techniques.
- List a technique only if the test's description explains, or plainly implies, how the control stops or reveals
  it. At most five.
- A test that implements a benchmark which publishes a mapping, such as CISA SCuBA, starts from that mapping and
  then applies these rules. An ID the pinned release has retired is replaced by its successor in that release,
   retired ATT&CK technique, carries a taxonomy tag, names a requirement that a shipped framework file does not
   have, or is a CIS or CISA test without a `Control` for its own framework.
2. **Attribute review** runs on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes. A
   reviewer model reads the test, its Markdown file and this page, and fails the check when a value does not fit
   the rubric, with the value it expected and the reason. It also sees the attributes of the other tests with the
   same product and feature. It fails a test whose area, resource type or severity differs from the same check in
   another suite, and whose user impact or implementation cost differs when both plainly recommend the same fix.
   MITRE techniques and related products are not compared. A maintainer can overrule it.
3. **Reviewers**, human or agent, apply the same page. See `AGENTS.md`.

## Review: PRs 2688, 2689, 2704, 2672 (Dfrank77)

All four PRs are mergeable, CI is green (attribute-review passes), and every CodeRabbit thread is resolved. The IDs MT.1261 to MT.1264 were reserved on #697 (2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02) and no other open PR uses them. `merill` has not commented on any of the four. There is one open question for him: on 2688 Dfrank77 asked "families, or one fixed severity and only list the role?" He'll apply the answer to all four risk tests.

The answer I'd give him is to keep single-result tests and drop the severity raise. As families, a clean tenant has no instances, so it gets `Skipped/NoInstances` instead of a Pass. A family also writes one row per risky user, which churns every run.

### Family recommendation (applies to 2688/2689/2704)
- **Keep four IDs.** They have different default severities, and folding them into one test with a `RiskLevel` parameter would lose that. A shim can't help either, because a shim must carry the same Severity as the test it calls.
- **Share the code instead.** The ~45-line privileged-role lookup is now copied four times (MT.1260/1261/1262/1263, roughly lines 80-125 in each). Move it to `powershell/internal/services/entra/`:
  - `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleByPrincipal -PrincipalId`
  - optionally `Get-MtUnremediatedRiskyIdentity -Kind User|ServicePrincipal -RiskLevel`
  
  The promised follow-up for group-inherited roles then becomes a one-place fix.
- **Fix MT.1260 on main.** `tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1260.ps1:154` passes `-Severity 'High'`, which is ignored in a single-result native test. Lines 10, 79 and 132 and `Test.MT.1260.md:7` still claim a raise. MT.1260 also lacks what MT.1261 adds: the `isDeleted` filter, the `Cloud` gate and the `RoleManagement.Read.*` permission.

### 2688 (MT.1261, medium-risk users): CHANGES
The code is correct. It uses v1.0 `riskyUsers` with the default paging and cache, has no outer try/catch, and gates on `AAD_PREMIUM_P2`. The permission is already in the preview scopes, the output goes through `Get-MtSafeMarkdown`, and the unit tests are good. The attributes fit the rubric (Low/Low/Low is right for a medium-risk user). The only real problem is drift from its sibling: this PR already touches `Test.MT.1260.md`, so it is the place to bring MT.1260 in line with MT.1261.

Defects:
- `Test.MT.1260.ps1:154`, plus lines 10/79/132 and `.md:7`: the dead severity raise.
- MT.1260 is missing `isDeleted`, `Cloud` and the RoleManagement permission.
- `Test.MT.1261.ps1` ~85-125: duplicated role lookup.

## Review: PRs 2688, 2689, 2704, 2672 (Dfrank77)

All four PRs are mergeable, CI is green (attribute-review passes), and every CodeRabbit thread is resolved. The IDs MT.1261 to MT.1264 were reserved on #697 (2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02) and no other open PR uses them. `merill` has not commented on any of the four. There is one open question for him: on 2688 Dfrank77 asked "families, or one fixed severity and only list the role?" He'll apply the answer to all four risk tests.

The answer I'd give him is to keep single-result tests and drop the severity raise. As families, a clean tenant has no instances, so it gets `Skipped/NoInstances` instead of a Pass. A family also writes one row per risky user, which churns every run.

### Family recommendation (applies to 2688/2689/2704)
- **Keep four IDs.** They have different default severities, and folding them into one test with a `RiskLevel` parameter would lose that. A shim can't help either, because a shim must carry the same Severity as the test it calls.
- **Share the code instead.** The ~45-line privileged-role lookup is now copied four times (MT.1260/1261/1262/1263, roughly lines 80-125 in each). Move it to `powershell/internal/services/entra/`:
  - `Get-MtPrivilegedRoleByPrincipal -PrincipalId`
  - optionally `Get-MtUnremediatedRiskyIdentity -Kind User|ServicePrincipal -RiskLevel`
  
  The promised follow-up for group-inherited roles then becomes a one-place fix.
- **Fix MT.1260 on main.** `tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1260.ps1:154` passes `-Severity 'High'`, which is ignored in a single-result native test. Lines 10, 79 and 132 and `Test.MT.1260.md:7` still claim a raise. MT.1260 also lacks what MT.1261 adds: the `isDeleted` filter, the `Cloud` gate and the `RoleManagement.Read.*` permission.

### 2688 (MT.1261, medium-risk users): CHANGES
The code is correct. It uses v1.0 `riskyUsers` with the default paging and cache, has no outer try/catch, and gates on `AAD_PREMIUM_P2`. The permission is already in the preview scopes, the output goes through `Get-MtSafeMarkdown`, and the unit tests are good. The attributes fit the rubric (Low/Low/Low is right for a medium-risk user). The only real problem is drift from its sibling: this PR already touches `Test.MT.1260.md`, so it is the place to bring MT.1260 in line with MT.1261.

Defects:
- `Test.MT.1260.ps1:154`, plus lines 10/79/132 and `.md:7`: the dead severity raise.
- MT.1260 is missing `isDeleted`, `Cloud` and the RoleManagement permission.
- `Test.MT.1261.ps1` ~85-125: duplicated role lookup.

### 2704 (MT.1263, medium-risk service principals): CHANGES
It is the same code as 2689, so the same helper ask applies. There is one attribute failure: `Test.MT.1263.ps1:28` sets `ImplementationCost = 'Low'`, but MT.1262 uses `Medium` for the identical fix. Both say to investigate, rotate credentials and dismiss. ### 2672 (MT.1264, Secure Score family): MERGE-WITH-NIT
This is a well-built family with the instance source in the same file, which the docs allow.
- It reads only the latest snapshot (`$top=1` with `-DisablePaging`, no cache bypass).
- It joins to the control profiles and keeps a scored control that has no profile as an Error instead of dropping it.
- It respects portal states, uses per-instance Product/Feature with keys that exist in the taxonomy, and notes the overlap with MT.1024.
- `SecurityEvents.Read.All` is in the preview scopes, and the earlier PSScriptAnalyzer `New-*` warnings are gone.

It doesn't duplicate an existing check: like MT.1024, it feeds results from an external tool, and MT.1266 (#2712) covers Azure secure score, which is a separate product. The attributes passed review. Points-only severity is reasonable given Dfrank77's point that some controls return rank 0.

Nits:
- `Test.MT.1264.ps1` ~59/70: the raw `controlName` is used as the instance `Id`. One name that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$` would turn the whole family into `InvalidInstanceId`. Sanitise it, or skip names that fail the pattern.
- ~24-28: calling `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotAuthorized` inside the instance source has no effect (the parent row becomes NoInstances), and the `Permission` gate already covers this case. Let it throw.
